records.rationale: Opening jurisprudence on MF-201. The instance read the provision — customer information is encrypted in transit and at rest; a change that weakens or removes encryption on a customer-data path requires the ciso's written finding of an effective alternative control. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-202. The instance read the provision — multi-factor authentication protects every individual's access to every information system; any exception requires a written, ciso-approved compensating control reviewed at least annually. — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on MF-203. The instance read the provision — no change disables or delays the telemetry that feeds regulatory incident reporting. — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-204. The instance read the provision — no ict third party enters a critical-or-important function path without a register-of-information entry, a documented exit strategy, and disclosure of subcontracting. — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-205. The instance read the provision — a change to a critical-or-important function is resilience tested before release; designated functions additionally carry threat-led penetration testing every three years. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-206. The instance read the provision — no credential, key, or token appears in source, configuration, or ci logs; secrets live in the vault. — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-207. The instance read the provision — every script on a payment page is authorized, inventoried, and integrity-checked, and a tamper-detection mechanism watches the page. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-208. The instance read the provision — no production change to a cardholder or ledger system without documented approval, a tested rollback, and separation between author and approver. — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-209. The instance read the provision — deploys are blocked on a greater-than-10% p95 latency regression, or any availability regression, on the payment-authorization path. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-210. The instance read the provision — personal data is collected for a stated purpose and deleted on schedule; no new personal-data field is retained without a recorded retention decision. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-211. The instance read the provision — no third-party code enters a cardholder-data or personal-data path without a completed vendor security review. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-212. The instance read the provision — no production deploy during a designated market-close or peak-period change freeze except under the emergency protocol. — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-301. The instance read the provision — no model reaches a credit, fraud, or aml decision in production before independent validation covering conceptual soundness, outcomes analysis, and ongoing monitoring. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-302. The instance read the provision — every model in a decision path carries an inventory entry and current documentation: purpose, training data, known limits, and a named owner. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-303. The instance read the provision — a customer interacting with an ai system is told so, and synthetic content the firm generates is machine-markable. — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-304. The instance read the provision — creditworthiness and credit-scoring systems are annex iii high-risk: risk management, data governance, logging, human oversight, and accuracy obligations must be in place before the applicable date. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-305. The instance read the provision — a decisioning model is tested for disparate impact across protected classes before deployment and monitored afterwards. — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-306. The instance read the provision — an ai-facing surface does not deceive a customer, impersonate a human, manufacture confidence it does not have, or steer a customer against their own interest. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-307. The instance read the provision — every agent-authored change carries a provenance attestation — agent identity, model version, and a link to the originating human requirement — and every agent action in production runs under an explicit value and rate bound. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-308. The instance read the provision — no customer personal data enters model training, or a third party model provider's retention window, without a lawful basis and a contractual carve-out. — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-401. The instance read the provision — no dark pattern, no material omission, and no fee or term a reasonable consumer would not expect from the disclosure given. — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-402. The instance read the provision — data furnished to consumer reporting agencies is accurate, disputes are investigated within the statutory window, and adverse action notices name both the reasons and the agency. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-403. The instance read the provision — cost-of-credit disclosures are accurate, timely, and in the required form before the consumer becomes bound. — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-404. The instance read the provision — opt-out of sale or sharing, and limits on sensitive personal information, are honoured on every surface including newly built ones. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-405. The instance read the provision — consumer-permissioned data access is built to a documented interface with revocable authorization, whatever shape the rule finally takes. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-406. The instance read the provision — consumer complaints are logged, routed, and closed within the stated window, and no change removes a complaint path without an equivalent replacement. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-520. The instance read the provision — screening lists are refreshed from the authoritative publication within the declared interval, and the interval is a constitutional parameter rather than a service setting — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-521. The instance read the provision — a change to a fuzzy-matching threshold, transliteration table, or name-normalisation rule is validated against a labelled set and recorded before release — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-522. The instance read the provision — a transaction-monitoring rule is retired only on a documented tuning study showing the coverage it carried is carried elsewhere — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-523. The instance read the provision — beneficial-ownership information is collected and verified before a legal-entity account is funded — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-524. The instance read the provision — originator and beneficiary information accompanies a qualifying funds transfer for its whole journey — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on MF-525. The instance read the provision — an alert backlog is aged, reported, and escalated; no change may suppress the ageing metric — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-526. The instance read the provision — a change to the cardholder-data environment scope is documented and the environment reassessed before release — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-527. The instance read the provision — every script on a payment page carries a recorded justification for its presence, not only an integrity check — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-528. The instance read the provision — segmentation between the cardholder-data environment and the corporate network is tested on any change that touches the boundary — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on MF-529. The instance read the provision — key-generation, loading and destruction ceremonies are dual-controlled and logged — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-530. The instance read the provision — deprecated cryptographic primitives — md5, sha-1, des, 3des, rc4 — are refused on any new or changed path — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on MF-531. The instance read the provision — every ingress and egress path enforces tls 1.2 or above with forward secrecy — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-532. The instance read the provision — key rotation intervals are declared per key class and enforced by the platform, not by convention — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on MF-534. The instance read the provision — a signed software bill of materials in spdx or cyclonedx form is produced for every build — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-535. The instance read the provision — build provenance meets slsa build level 3: hermetic, ephemeral runners and a signed attestation naming the source and the steps — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-536. The instance read the provision — every package declared in a manifest resolves in an approved registry before the build advances; a name that resolves nowhere fails the build — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-539. The instance read the provision — a dependency carrying a cve above the declared cvss threshold blocks the merge unless an explicit, time-bound risk-acceptance waiver is attached — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-540. The instance read the provision — changed-line test coverage meets the declared floor on payment, ledger and decisioning services — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-541. The instance read the provision — a tested rollback exists and has been exercised for every production change on a regulated surface — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-543. The instance read the provision — a feature flag on a regulated surface defaults closed, and no change may invert that default without amendment — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-544. The instance read the provision — every mutable payment endpoint requires an idempotency key, and a repeated submission returns the original result rather than executing again — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-545. The instance read the provision — a transaction rolls back completely under injected mid-transaction failure, and the isolation level under which it does so is declared and tested — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-546. The instance read the provision — concurrent debits against one account are serialised so that no interleaving permits a double spend — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-547. The instance read the provision — reconciliation breaks are aged, reported and escalated; no change may suppress a break or reset its age — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-548. The instance read the provision — an event-sourced history is immutable under replay: the same event stream reproduces the same balances — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-554. The instance read the provision — a circuit breaker opens on downstream failure so that the caller fails fast rather than hanging, and every outbound call declares a timeout — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-557. The instance read the provision — concentration risk in an ict provider is recorded before the provider enters a further critical path — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-558. The instance read the provision — deletion and cryptographic-shredding paths exist and are exercised for every new personal-data store — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-559. The instance read the provision — a data-protection impact assessment is completed before new high-risk processing begins — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on MF-560. The instance read the provision — a sub-processor's processing region is declared before data flows to it — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-562. The instance read the provision — outcome parity across protected classes is measured and documented before deployment and monitored afterwards; a parity exception is time-boxed and carries a named owner — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on MF-563. The instance read the provision — ongoing monitoring thresholds are declared before deployment and are not removed after it — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-564. The instance read the provision — a champion model is replaced only on a recorded comparison against the challenger on the same population — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-565. The instance read the provision — an override of a model decision is logged with the reason and the identity of the person who made it — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-566. The instance read the provision — an adverse action notice is issued within the statutory window and names both the principal reasons and the agency consulted — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-567. The instance read the provision — every ai system carries an inventory entry recording its intended purpose and its risk classification — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-568. The instance read the provision — human oversight is operable and tested rather than nominal: the reviewer can see the basis of a decision and can stop it — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-571. The instance read the provision — an agent-authored change to security policy, rbac, or a decisioning path requires multiparty human review — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-573. The instance read the provision — a fee or term is stated where a consumer will see it before the binding moment, not only in a linked schedule — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-574. The instance read the provision — cancellation of a recurring product is at least as easy as sign-up and available on the same surface — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-576. The instance read the provision — a privileged action is attributable to a named individual; no privileged path runs under a shared account — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-577. The instance read the provision — evidence export for an examiner is reproducible from the audit store without manual assembly — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-578. The instance read the provision — log clocks are synchronised to a trusted source, and a change may not widen the permitted drift — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-590. The instance read the provision — a risk acceptance carries an expiry and a referral, and lapses on time whether or not the referral has been answered — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on MF-591. The instance read the provision — a renewal of a lapsed acceptance is visible on the record and never silent — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-592. The instance read the provision — ordinary and absolute status is stated on the face of the rule, not inferred from severity — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-593. The instance read the provision — a change to a gate threshold is routed to the amendment channel, never applied in place — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-594. The instance read the provision — the constitution declares whether any party holds contest standing adverse to grants — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-595. The instance read the provision — reporter output never reaches the adjudication input path, and the audit register is never read by resolve — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on MF-596. The instance read the provision — every arrival that is not charged leaves exactly one docket entry — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-602. The instance read the provision — a credit transfer in euro is checked against the payee's name before the payer confirms it, the match result is shown to the payer, and no batch, bulk or retry path skips the check — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-604. The instance read the provision — a request for payment carries a verified sender, and an instant-rail transfer is fraud-scored before settlement with a recall path that survives a change to the rail integration — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-605. The instance read the provision — the identity-theft prevention programme's red-flag rules run on every covered account and application, each detection has a documented response, and no channel is exempted by configuration — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-606. The instance read the provision — high-risk actions — credential reset, payee addition, limit increase, address change — require a step-up challenge whose strength matches the risk, and no recovery path reintroduces a bypass — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-607. The instance read the provision — applicant identity elements are verified against an authoritative source and scored for synthetic-identity indicators before an account is funded, including thin-file and no-file applicants — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-609. The instance read the provision — an account for an applicant the record shows to be under eighteen is opened only with a verified adult custodian, and personal information is not collected online from a child under thirteen without verifiable parental consent — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-610. The instance read the provision — before a disclosure the law requires in writing is delivered electronically instead of on paper, the consumer's informed consent is captured with the hardware and software statement, and the consent stays withdrawable — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-611. The instance read the provision — no autodialed call, prerecorded or artificial-voice message, or automated text reaches a wireless number without recorded prior express consent for that purpose, written where the purpose is marketing, and revocation is honoured on every channel — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-612. The instance read the provision — a privacy notice is delivered before nonpublic personal information is shared outside the exceptions, the opt-out reaches every disclosure path, and reliance on the annual-notice exception is checked against its conditions — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-613. The instance read the provision — debt-collection contact frequency stays inside the presumptive seven-calls-in-seven-days limit and the seven-day post-conversation limit, a cease request stops the channel, and validation information precedes collection activity — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on MF-614. The instance read the provision — deposit account fees, the annual percentage yield and its computation method are disclosed before the account is opened, and a change in terms that reduces the yield or adds a fee is noticed before it takes effect — and held deny on the recorded premise.

The instance read the provision — dormancy periods, owner due-diligence notices and remittance deadlines are read from the governing state's unclaimed-property table, and no internal system event resets an account's dormancy clock — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

The instance read the provision — the path by which suspected financial exploitation of an older or vulnerable customer is escalated, held where state law permits, and reported stays reachable from the servicing case and is never downgraded to a passive report — and held permit on the recorded premise.

The instance read the provision — a data-subject access request is answered within one month and a portability request produces a structured, commonly used, machine-readable export; an extension is notified with its reasons rather than taken silently — and held permit on the recorded premise.
